memoryText: Come to me, all who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read Matthew 11:28 slowly, several times, and then say it from memory. Read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
This invitation comes right after Jesus has condemned cities that would not repent, and right after he has said that the Father has revealed these things to little children. It is addressed to people who know they are tired.

“Come to me.” Jesus does not say, “Come to a system,” or “Come to my teaching.” He says, “Come to me.” Rest is found in a person. The invitation is personal, direct, and present. You are not asked to improve first.

“All who labor and are heavy laden.” “Labor” means to be worn out from toil, and “heavy laden” means loaded down. It includes the weariness of trying to earn God’s favor, the weight of guilt, the burden of grief, and the sheer tiredness of life in a fallen world. The invitation is for “all.” No one is excluded.

“And I will give you rest.” The word “give” is crucial. Rest is a gift. It is not wages. Jesus gives soul rest: peace with God, relief from the need to prove ourselves, and a settled place in him. In the next verses, he says that his yoke is easy and his burden light.

This verse is for the weary Christian as well as the seeker. Keep it near. When you are exhausted by life or by trying to be good enough, hear him say it to you again: Come.
weekInReview: This week you followed Jesus through the Sermon’s conclusion and into his works. You learned from Psalm 1 and Matthew 7 that there are two roads and two foundations. In Psalms 146 and 147, you praised the God who helps the helpless and heals the brokenhearted, and in Matthew 8 and 9 you saw Jesus do exactly that: cleansing a leper, calming a storm, forgiving a paralytic, and raising a girl. You saw him send out the Twelve, answer John’s doubt with works, and invite the weary to come to him. You watched the opposition grow as he declared himself Lord of the Sabbath, and you heard the parable of the sower. Psalm 78 reminded you to pass the stories of God’s deeds to the next generation.
reflectionQuestions: Jesus said, “Come to me, all who labor and are heavy laden.” What weights are you carrying that you have not yet brought to him?
Jesus forgave the paralytic’s sins before healing his body. Why do you think he started there, and what does that say about our deepest need?
The parable of the sower asks what kind of soil we are. What is one practical way you can prepare your heart to receive and keep the word this week?
prayerPrompts: Come to Jesus tired and burdened, and thank him for the rest he gives.
Ask him to heal what is broken.
Ask him to forgive what needs forgiving.
